q: Mein on()-Trigger im JavaScript-Adapter feuert nicht, wenn ein Datenpunkt per expire abläuft bzw. gelöscht wird, und auch nicht, wenn das Gerät einen Wert mit Qualitätscode ungleich 0 liefert. Was muss ich im Trigger-Pattern angeben?
facts: standardmäßig werden nur States mit Qualität q=0 (0x00) an den Callback geliefert; mit q: '*' im Pattern kommen alle Qualitätscodes
für Löschungen/Expires als Trigger muss change 'ne' oder 'any' UND q: '*' gesetzt sein, z. B. on({id: '...', change: 'any', q: '*'}, cb)
evidence: ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: By default only states with quality 0x00 will be passed to callback function. If you want to get all events, add `{q: '*'}` to pattern structure.
ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: If you want to also get state deletions/expires as trigger, you need to use change with `ne` or `any` AND q with `*` as filter!

q: In the javascript adapter I want script A to ask script B for data and get a reply, and I also want to call the same handler from my own adapter. Which functions do I use, what is the default reply timeout, and how does the call from another adapter look?
facts: receiver registers onMessage('messageName', (data, callback) => { ... callback(result); })
sender uses messageTo({instance, script, message} or just 'messageName', data, {timeout}, callback) or messageToAsync; default callback timeout is 5000 ms (5 s)
from another adapter: sendTo('javascript.0', 'toScript', {script: 'script.js.<name>', message: 'messageName', data: {...}})
only the first response is accepted, further answers are ignored

ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: Callback and options are optional and timeout is by default 5000 milliseconds (if callback provided).
ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: adapter.sendTo('javascript.0', 'toScript', {
ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: The response from script which sends response as first will be accepted as answer, all other answers will be ignored.

q: Ich will mit compareTime prüfen, ob es gerade mindestens 30 Minuten nach Sonnenuntergang ist und noch nicht 30 Minuten vor Sonnenaufgang. Wie gebe ich Astro-Zeiten mit Offset an und welche Vergleichsoperationen gibt es?
facts: compareTime(startTime, endTime, operation, timeToCompare); ohne timeToCompare wird die aktuelle Zeit verwendet

Operationen: '>', '>=', '<', '<=', '==', '<>', 'between', 'not between'

q: formatTimeDiff in my script prints '51:09:15' for a duration of a bit over two days. What is the default format, how do I get days shown separately, and how can I put literal words like 'Days' into the format string?
facts: with format null the default 'hh:mm:ss' is used and hours are not wrapped at 24 (e.g. 51:09:15)
use the day tokens DD/D (or TT/T), e.g. formatTimeDiff(diff, 'DD hh:mm') -> '02 03:09'
literal characters are escaped with backslash \, e.g. 'DD \Day\s, h \hour\s'

ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: formatTimeDiff(diff, 'DD hh:mm'); // "02 03:09"
ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: You can use escape charachter `\` to avoid the replacement.

q: I forward error logs to Telegram with onLog('error', ...) in a script, but console.error inside the handler never shows up in the log. Why? And how do I remove such a log handler later?
facts: inside an onLog handler you cannot output logs with the same severity (prevents infinite loops)
with onLog('*', ...) log output inside the handler is disabled completely
onLogUnregister(id) with the id returned by onLog, or with the handler function, or with a severity like 'warn'

ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: // or unsubscribe all handlers with specific severity

q: In jsonConfig, how do I show a COM-port field only when the host runs Windows and a hint text only when ioBroker itself runs in Docker? Is it the browser's OS that counts, and what happens to the value of a hidden field?

q: Scripts call sendTo() on my own adapter, but my adapter never gets the messages, and after fixing that the scripts hang waiting for an answer. What is needed in io-package.json, how do I reply correctly, and what happens to the callback if someone sends to 'myadapter' without an instance number?
facts: io-package.json needs common.messagebox: true, otherwise sendTo messages silently disappear
in onMessage(obj) always reply when obj.callback is set: this.sendTo(obj.from, obj.command, result, obj.callback), passing obj.from and obj.callback unchanged
sendTo to an adapter without instance number (e.g. 'pushover') goes to all instances and the callback is ignored

ioBroker.docs/docs/de/dev/messagebox.md :: this.sendTo(obj.from, obj.command, { sent: true }, obj.callback);
ioBroker.docs/docs/de/dev/messagebox.md :: **Immer antworten, wenn `obj.callback` gesetzt ist.**
ioBroker.js-controller/packages/controller/doc/classes/AdapterClass.md :: If no instance given (e.g. "pushover"), the callback argument will be ignored. Because normally many responses will come.

q: tr-064 adapter: the callmonitor states stay empty and callmonitor.connected is false. What do I have to do on the Fritz!Box side, which port is involved, and will the monitor also show when my door intercom calls my phones internally via **9?
facts: the call monitor must be switched on in the Fritz!Box by dialing #96*5* on a connected phone (#96*4* switches it off)
the Fritz!Box then opens TCP port 1012
internal calls (e.g. a door bell calling **9) are not reported by the Fritz!Box, neither to the call monitor nor via TR-064

q: My backitup web UI isn't reachable anymore after an SD card crash. How do I restore a backitup ioBroker backup manually on the console, what do I have to run afterwards, and how do I get the CCU backup that backitup also made back onto my RaspberryMatic?

q: Ich habe in der javascript-Instanz die Option "Nicht alle Zustände beim Start abonnieren" aktiviert, um RAM zu sparen. Seitdem funktionieren Skripte mit getState('id').val nicht mehr. Warum, und wie muss ich die Skripte umschreiben?
facts: mit der Option abonniert der Adapter nur noch die IDs, für die on()/subscribe aufgerufen wird, und hält nicht alle State-Werte im RAM
getState kann dann nicht synchron verwendet werden – der Wert muss aus der zentralen States-Datenbank geholt werden
Lösung: getState mit Callback (getState(id, (err, state) => ...)) oder Promise (z. B. getStateAsync) verwenden, oder die Option wieder deaktivieren
evidence: ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: Adapter subscribes every time on specified ID when `on/subscribe` is called. In this mode, the adapter receives only updates for desired states. This option requires less RAM and is more efficient, but you cannot access states synchronously via getState. **You must use callbacks or promises to access the states**
ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.javascript/javascript.md :: Reason: The adapter does not have the state's value in RAM and must request it from the central state database.
ioBroker.javascript/src/lib/sandbox.ts :: Please disable that setting or use "getState" with a callback, e.g.: getState('${id}', (err, state) => { ... });

q: With the harmony adapter, how do I start and stop an activity from a script, and what do the numeric values of activities.currentStatus mean? Also, what value should I write to a device function to send a single short key press?
facts: start: write a number > 0 to {instance}.{hub name}.activities.{activity}; it changes to 1 (starting) then 2 (active)
stop: set the activity to 0 (or write any number to activities.currentStatus)
currentStatus: 0 = inactive, 1 = starting, 2 = active, 3 = stopping
device functions take a value in milliseconds; 1-250 ms usually sends a single key press (>250 ms may trigger several times)
evidence: ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.harmony/README.md :: An activity is started by entering a number greater than 0 at the activity `{instance}.{hub name}.activities.{activity}`. While the activity is being executed, this value first changes to 1 (= starting) and then to 2 (= active).

ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.harmony/README.md :: Running activities are stopped by setting their value to 0. Alternatively, any number can be entered in the object `{instance}.{hub name}.activities.currentStatus` to stop the running activity.
ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.harmony/README.md :: - 0 = inactive - 1 = starting - 2 = active - 3 = stopping

ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.harmony/README.md :: Values have the unit `milliseconds`. If a value between 1 and 250 ms is entered, the Harmony hub usually sends a single key press of the given length. Values greater than 250 ms can lead to the device function being triggered several times.

q: Ich möchte alte Zählerwerte mit eigenen Zeitstempeln nachträglich in die History (bzw. InfluxDB/SQL) schreiben, z. B. aus einer CSV. Gibt es dafür einen sendTo-Befehl, welche Formate akzeptiert er, und bedeutet eine erfolgreiche Antwort, dass die Daten wirklich geschrieben wurden?
facts: sendTo('<instanz>', 'storeState', ...) – z. B. history.0, funktioniert auch für influxdb/sql
drei Formate: eine id mit einem state-Objekt; eine id mit einem Array von states; ein Array aus mehreren {id, state}-Objekten
state enthält u. a. ts (Zeitstempel in ms), val, ack, from
eine erfolgreiche Antwort heißt nur, dass die Daten verarbeitet wurden, nicht dass sie wirklich geschrieben wurden

ioBroker.docs/docs/de/adapterref/iobroker.history/README.md :: Eine erfolgreiche Antwort heißt nicht, dass auch wirklich Daten geschrieben wurden. Es bedeutet nur, dass die Daten erfolgreich verarbeitet wurden!

q: openknx adapter: which physical KNX address should I give the adapter (can I use the gateway's own address?), what's the usual port, and what setting should I change when the log keeps showing DISCONNECT_REQUEST errors?
facts: the physical KNX address (e.g. 1.1.250) must be configured as an additional address of the IP interface in ETS and must not be used by another device
port is normally 3671 (filled in by Detect)
increase 'Minimum send delay between two frames [ms]', e.g. to 80-150 ms, to avoid flooding the bus

ioBroker.docs/docs/en/adapterref/iobroker.openknx/README.md :: **Port** -- normally 3671. Filled in automatically by detection.

q: Multihost with the states DB in Redis on the master: the slave gets `connect ECONNREFUSED 192.168.1.10:6379` for the states DB while objects work. Redis on the master is version 7. What has to be changed?
facts: In /etc/redis/redis.conf on the master, extend `bind 127.0.0.1` with the master's LAN IP (e.g. `bind 127.0.0.1 192.168.1.10`) or use `bind 0.0.0.0` – only needed on the master
From Redis 7 on, protected mode must also be disabled: `protected-mode no`
